author: ojiudezue
title: URA is going to more homes: no Carrier/house quirks in shared paths
summary: Operator is rolling URA out to other homes ('Not everyone has a Bryant variable speed'). The thermostat-brand abstraction (W1-C) is unparked; Batch C lands Custom Preset Ranges as a Carrier-profile capability (strategy supplies the service; GenericStrategy returns unsupported). Single-install 'no back-compat' assumption is now time-limited.
why: Carrier-specific assumptions live in shared code: borrows bypass the strategy, override detection keys on preset_mode == manual, Carrier timings, named-preset holds, ODU telemetry features. Each blocks a second brand.
implications: Designs must put device quirks behind profiles/config. Once a second install exists, stored-config changes need real migrations. W1-C plan (inventory + profile design + phased Carrier-byte-identical P1) is the next HVAC planning item; the planner run hit the usage limit and must be restarted.
revisit_trigger: A second thermostat brand available to test; first non-Carrier install.
